bullets.title: NVDA: Jensen Huang resignation triggers downgrades, $500B market cap loss, but retail dip-buys aggressively
bullets.body: Jensen Huang resigned as NVIDIA CEO amid DOJ probe/extramarital affair reports; Colette Kress named interim CEO. Multiple sell-side cuts followed: HSBC downgraded to Hold, cut PT to $170 from $365; GS cut PT to $220 from $300; MS cut PT to $267 from $300 on 10% China estimate haircut; Bernstein downgraded to Market-Perform at $200. Stock traded down ~40% from Oct highs but bounced off ~$150, with retail buying $111M in first 30 min Thursday (~40x normal) — JPM noted a ~9 sigma retail buying event. Street consensus: fundamentals intact at ~10x CY27 EPS (~$15.60), but Kress's opposition to Huang's $250B OpenAI backstop and neocloud financing raises ecosystem risk. NVDA earnings Tuesday post-market remain the next major catalyst.

bullets.title: NVDA: China export control tightening, Megaspeed/DOJ probe broadening political risk
bullets.body: Jensen Huang's exit accelerates Commerce Dept. finalization of tighter compute-access restrictions across seven additional countries. Congressional probe into Nvidia chip sales to China expected to run into next year; Lutnick to testify. Megaspeed (alleged chip diversion conduit) now lawyered up. Alice Huang-linked firms reportedly promised DeepSeek Nvidia chips; DOJ also probing SMCI on related smuggling allegations. MATCH Act represents greatest escalation risk to US-China tech truce.

bullets.title: CSCO: Strong Q1 beat; AI revenue guided to $9B in FY27 (+125% YoY), but product orders decelerating
bullets.body: CSCO Q1 revenue $18.52B beat by ~$400M (all from networking >$11B); EPS $1.40 beat by 5.3%. FY27 guidance raised: revenue $74.8-75.8B, EPS $5.47-5.53 (vs. prior FS $5.10), AI infrastructure revenue to $9B (>2x FY26, 12% of total). Product orders +21% YoY but decelerated from +35% last quarter; campus orders slowed to +14% from +20%. Gross margins expected to compress in 2H FY27 as hyperscaler mix rises. Security ex-Splunk +15%, firewalls +30% for third consecutive quarter. MS maintains Equal-Weight at $120 PT; Citi cuts to $120 from $139 (Buy); Wells Fargo to $130 from $150 (OW). Stock -2.6% pre-market on order deceleration concerns despite strong print.

bullets.title: FOXA: Morgan Stanley names Top Pick, $90 PT (37% upside) post-Roku deal close
bullets.body: MS resumes Overweight and elevates FOXA to Top Pick following early close of $22B Roku acquisition. Pro forma revenue growth lifts to ~6% (from low-singles); EBITDA CAGR rises to ~9% from ~1% (CY27-30E); FCF/share compounds at ~20% through FY30. Combined Fox/Tubi/Roku Channel holds 10%+ of monthly US TV viewing, rivaling Disney and ahead of Netflix. $400M+ cost synergies modeled; $500M-$1B revenue synergies excluded from base case. Net leverage falls from 2.8x to ~1x by FY29. Bull/bear: $100/$60; consensus PT $79.33.

bullets.title: HUBS: Co-founder Halligan returns as CEO; leadership reset signals AI refounding, near-term uncertainty
bullets.body: CEO Yamini Rangan steps down immediately; co-founder Brian Halligan returns as CEO after five years, citing need to overhaul product, culture, and sales processes. CFO Kate Bueker retiring Feb 2027; Adobe CFO Karen Burgess named replacement. Q4 and FY26 guidance reaffirmed but future RIFs not ruled out. Mizuho maintains Outperform, $240 PT ($215.84 current). MS and Citi flag near-term margin/growth uncertainty around the strategic reset toward agentic AI.

bullets.title: RBLX: Citi downgrades to Neutral; GTA VI launch risk + fading Steal An Egg threaten 4Q guidance
bullets.body: Citi cuts RBLX from Buy to Neutral, maintaining $55 PT (28x 2028 FCF). Steal An Egg CCU down ~56% from September peak with no breakout replacement; GTA VI launches Nov 19, poses engagement risk management can't yet size. MTD November CCUs suggest 4Q26 bookings of $1.92B, slightly below guidance midpoint of $1.95B. Stock -5.7% pre-market.

bullets.title: IONQ: Gains high-profile CFO hire from CVLT; quantum computing narrative building
bullets.body: IonQ named Gary Merrill (current Commvault CFO) as CFO effective early December; Inder Singh stepping down immediately. KeyBanc flagged the departure as negative for CVLT given Merrill's influence on GTM organization; CVLT reaffirmed F3Q and FY27 guidance, $200 PT maintained. AMD also expanding quantum computing partnership with PsiQuantum.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone Duo seeing >30% return rates; on-device AI already lagging competitors
bullets.body: More than 30% of iPhone Duo buyers returned the product citing lack of Face ID, camera quality, form factor, and durability concerns. Apple's on-device AI capabilities already lagging emerging personal assistants like Muse per channel checks. AAPL hit a 52-week high at $360 (+31.6% YTD) despite the product headwinds flagged.

bullets.title: INTU: JPM maintains Neutral; valuation cheap at 10x uFCF but recovery unsustainable without customer acquisition improvement
bullets.body: JPM previews INTU F1Q27 (reports soon): revenue forecast $4.297B (+11% YoY), slightly below guidance midpoint; PF EPS $2.50 (21% margin). Management strategy sacrifices near-term ARPC growth for entry-level customer acquisition, but new customer additions across QuickBooks and TurboTax DIY remain weak. JPM expects shares range-bound until revenue growth and new customer growth inflect; FY27 total revenue forecast $23.383B (+9%), below guidance midpoint.

bullets.title: AVGO: Downgraded to Neutral at Rothschild/Redburn, PT cut to $398 from $595; gaining from NVDA weakness
bullets.body: Rothschild & Co Redburn downgraded AVGO to Neutral with PT cut to $398 from $595. Despite the downgrade, AVGO gained ~$500B in combined market cap alongside AMD this week as capital rotated from NVDA. MS notes AVGO providing richer deal incentives (~75% vs 25%) in response to NVDA ecosystem financing pressures. Stock -2.3% pre-market on the Redburn downgrade.

bullets.title: MU/SMCI: Memory prices rising 15-20% QoQ on AI demand; SMCI under DOJ probe
bullets.body: Memory manufacturers planning 15-20% sequential enterprise SSD price increases in 4Q26; PC DRAM prices rising 13-18% despite weaker consumer demand — a positive for MU. Separately, DOJ is probing SMCI regarding suspected involvement of Alice Huang-related entities in smuggling products to China. Technical analysis suggests AI/memory/semis expected to work lower near-term.

bullets.title: NBIS: Citi raises FY27 revenue est. +14pts, shifts PT to $215; site delays are timing, not thesis
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy/High Risk on NBIS after Q3 beat; near-term revenue guidance trimmed on site delays at Vineland NJ and multiple 3P sites. Prepayments now cover >100% of associated capex; pricing/revenue per MW strengthening. FY27 revenue estimates up 14 points; EPS estimates down 19 points. Stock -1.9% to $126.16 pre-market.

bullets.title: TLN: Oppenheimer initiates at Outperform, $400 PT; 750MW LT capacity deal locks ~$100M/yr revenue
bullets.body: Oppenheimer initiates TLN at Outperform with $400 PT. TLN signed a 750MW long-term PJM capacity agreement for delivery years 2029/30-2035/36 generating ~$100M/yr. Base adjusted FCF/share guidance: ~$38/$48/$46-50 for 2027/28/2029E (~30% CAGR). Upside levers: new data center PPAs, faster AWS ramp, accretive M&A. Company executing $1.5B ASR with additional $1.5B authorized through 2028.

bullets.title: HOOD: October net deposits $15.1B beat Street; trading volumes modestly below, OW maintained at $135
bullets.body: KeyBanc raises conviction on HOOD: October net deposits of $15.1B beat ~$13B+ Street expectations; core deposits ex-Trump Accounts of $8.6B also beat. Event contracts ADV +7% vs. 3Q avg. Equities/options/crypto retail ADV lower vs. 3Q and September. Margin balances up 4% vs. September. KeyBanc maintains Overweight, $135 PT (46.4x FY27E P/E). Stock -1.1% pre-market.

bullets.title: PINS: ChatGPT Ads survey identifies Pinterest as clearest share donor in digital advertising
bullets.body: Roth survey of ad agencies found ChatGPT Ads reached ~$1B ARR with 10K+ advertisers (up from 600 in seven months). ROI perception rated middling — in line with Pinterest/Nextdoor, below Google/Instagram/TikTok. Pinterest identified as the clearest share donor, with more agencies planning to cut vs. add spend there in 2026-2027. Key open question: whether ChatGPT dollars are new spend or reallocation from GOOGL/META/AMZN.

bullets.title: SNDK: 8-for-1 stock split confirmed, ex-date November 20
bullets.body: SanDisk (SNDK) executing an 8-for-1 stock split with ex-date November 20, 2026; record date November 9, payable November 19, allocation November 21. Fractions paid in cash in lieu. Mandatory corporate action with due bill period.

bullets.title: META: Cambridge Analytica jury trial ordered in Washington D.C.
bullets.body: META is set to face a jury trial in Washington D.C. for allegedly misleading users over data privacy in connection with the Cambridge Analytica scandal. No financial estimates or rating actions accompanied the headline.

bullets.title: CHTR: $1.5B tender offer viewed as positive catalyst; debt trading at ~85% of par
bullets.body: Charter's tender offer of up to $1.5B is viewed as a positive catalyst per channel checks; company debt trading at ~85% of par represents embedded asset value. Starlink U.S. median speeds ~120mbps download with ~3M estimated subscribers, likely below consensus modeling — a modest competitive read-across.

bullets.title: CSCO/PANW/CRWD: Cybersecurity consolidation winners; PANW upgraded at KeyBanc, CRWD +3.4% pre-market
bullets.body: DA Davidson VAR survey shows CRWD with highest net sales performance in 4 years; OKTA fourth straight QoQ improvement; PANW Prisma SASE improving significantly with 74% of resellers exceeding practice expectations. PANW upgraded at KeyBanc (+3.7% pre-market); CRWD +3.4% on MSFT outage read-through. MS reseller survey shows security-practice growth expectations improved to +13% YoY; firewall orders at CSCO grew >30% for third consecutive quarter.

bullets.title: FOXA/WMG: FOXA named MS Top Pick; week-ahead includes DIS earnings Tuesday
bullets.body: Beyond the FOXA Top Pick call (see above), MS flags WMG as a top pick in media. DIS reports Tuesday alongside HD; BABA and WMT report Thursday. MSFT Ignite Conference also scheduled for Tuesday alongside NVDA earnings — a heavy catalyst week for the tech/media complex.
